messages:
sophie: Heads up — main CI flipped red right after the merge of #4321 (auth-cs fix). Failing stage: model-serve-smoke. Dashboard: https://ci.internal/jobs/7012346789 :eyes:

ci-bot: Build 7012346789 — FAILED in model-serve-smoke. Failure summary: alloc-fallback detected, latency spike (~10s per request), >1 test timeout. Logs excerpt below:

```
[2026-03-18T22:10:03Z] allocator: KVM alloc failed, falling back to host CPU
[2026-03-18T22:10:04Z] serve: startup latency 9.8s
[2026-03-18T22:10:05Z] smoke-test: TEST_TIMEOUT exceeded for test "health-check" (10s)
```

arjun: I can take first pass on logs and correlate with node events. grabbing logs now

liz: I merged #4321 — if this is infra allocation it's better to triage than revert. @arjun please check for any cgroup/limit changes in that PR. @ops-oncall fyi

mike: Quick grep I ran locally: `rg "alloc failed|fallback|cgroup" --no-line-number build/logs | head -n 20` shows a cluster of `OOM` followed by `fallback` around the same timestamps as the smoke failures

arjun: Confirming — allocator issued `fallback to CPU` for 3 pods on node gpu-prod-12 at 22:09:59. Node metrics show a transient pressure spike on /dev/nvidia0. Attaching short snippet from node-agent logs:

```
node-agent@gpu-prod-12: 22:09:58 GPU memory alloc fail: 1.2GiB free but fragmentation prevents allocation
node-agent@gpu-prod-12: 22:09:59 trigger: allocator fallback to CPU (policy=graceful)
node-agent@gpu-prod-12: 22:10:00 container restart (evicted)
```

ops-oncall: I'm on it — pulling up host telemetry and NV driver logs. If this is fragmentation we might need kernel reboots; will advise quickly

sophie: If fallback is what's causing timeouts, can we reproduce by forcing no-fallback? e.g., rerun with `FORCE_ALLOC_NO_FALLBACK=true` to see if smoke consistently fails or passes. That will tell us if it's infra or the new runtime behavior.

liz: I'll trigger a targeted rerun on the same commit with forced env now (pinning selectors to gpu-prod-13 to avoid gpu-prod-12). Starting rerun: https://ci.internal/runs/7012346795 — will report back

ci-bot: Rerun 7012346795 queued (target: commit abcdef1234, env: FORCE_ALLOC_NO_FALLBACK=true, node_selector=gpu-prod-13)

arjun: Meanwhile I'm starting a bisect across recent deploys between abc000..abcdef to see when allocator fallback began spiking. If it narrows to the PR, we revert; if not, infra ops take over.

mike: If bisect implicates #4321, recommend preparing a fast revert PR and open an incident ticket for infra so we don't block main traffic. If it's infra, we call a kernel/drivers patch window.

sophie: Good plan. Keep updates short here. If we don't have a determinative result in 15 mins, escalate to oncall+eng-sre. :thumbsup:

liz: Rerun started and first logs incoming. Early sign: same latency spike but fewer fallbacks (pinned node looks healthier). Uploading crash snippets in the run.

arjun: Update: bisect job 7012346820 started, will report earliest commit with repeatable fallback. If it pins to abcde8 (pre-#4321) then it's infra. If it's abcdef1234, we revert.

ops-oncall: NV driver logs show a firmware hiccup window at 22:09:45-22:10:10 on gpu-prod-12. I'm paging infra leads now.

sophie: Thanks all. Tagging this thread: we'll decide revert vs infra mitigation once bisect finishes. If you find an immediate short-term unblock (e.g., node cordon/replace), call it out and act.

(threads like this continue in the run logs — keep replies here concise)
